doc.title: Abe Most interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 13, 1999

title: Growing up in Manhattan and the Bronx; father the cap maker
summary: Abe was born in Manhattan and moved between the Bronx and Atlantic City; his father was a tailor who made caps.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Yes. I was born in Manhattan, then we vacillated back and forth from the Bronx to Atlantic City back to the Bronx. And that was about it. Last I remember we were back in the Bronx and my brother, who had taken my old instruments, clarinet, flute, etcetera, and I was out on the road, and he took over the local — whatever you take over locally.
Yeah. What was your father’s profession?

He was a cap maker, he was a tailor. He made those little — nowadays they’re specialty caps, you know, the little visor and — a cap. And occasionally he’d bring me one. And I don’t really know exactly — it’s funny I would like to have seen what he did, but after all these years, “What did you do?” “I made caps.” But I know he made these because he’d bring them home once in a while.
